name: Field Doctor-Style Cottage Pie (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
400 g Extra Lean Beef
400 g Potato
3 medium Sweet Potatoes
4 medium Carrots
225 g Kale Curly
1/4 x 400 g tins Plum Tomato
95 g Celeriac (CELERY)
1/4 medium Swedes
1 1/2 tbsp Tomato Puree [tomato]
28 g Peas
6.6 g Chives
2 tbsp Mixed Herbs
1 tsp Red Wine Vinegar
2/3 tsp Tamari [water, SOYA beans, sea salt]
1 1/4 tsp Tapioca Starch
3/4 tbsp Parsley Flat
3/4 tsp Beef Stock [Beef Extract, Water, Salt]
3.7 g Shiitake Mushrooms
1/4 tsp Sea Salt
1/3 tsp Nutmeg Ground
1/3 tsp Black Pepper
directions:
1. Mash topping: Boil potato and sweet potato until soft. Drain well, mash with extra virgin olive oil, chives, nutmeg, salt and pepper until smooth. Keep warm.

2. Filling: Brown extra-lean beef in extra virgin olive oil. Add diced carrot, celeriac, swede, shiitake and chives; cook until softening. Stir in chopped tomato, tomato puree, peas, kale, beef stock, tamari, red wine vinegar and herb mix. Simmer until rich; thicken with tapioca slurry. Season.

3. Assemble: Spread filling in oven dish(es), top with the mash, rough up the surface with a fork.

4. Bake: 190°C fan for 25–35 minutes until bubbling and golden on top. Rest briefly before portioning.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Water, Extra Lean Beef, Potato, Sweet Potato, Carrot, Kale Curly, Extra Virgin Olive Oil, Chopped Tomato...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Cottage Pie (Low FODMAP) (~401 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/cottage-pie
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~401 g x 8 = 3208 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~401 g (inferred ~12.49% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~94 g (inferred ~2.92% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
